subproblem.statement: Assume (MR) and (VO). (MR): M_W(X) = R.measure(W) whenever R is an IMRep representing X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, W open (verbatim the (MR) hypothesis of the selected node's frozen Lean statement, the mass identity of dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support). (VO): S(ω) = 0 for every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S (verbatim the (VO) hypothesis of the selected node, the frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support). Let P ∈ ℕ and let S ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with compact support. Then there are a finite set F ⊆ spt S and integers m(x) (x ∈ ℝ^P) such that S(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)·g(x)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g on ℝ^P, where g(x)⟨⟩ denotes the value of the 0-covector g(x) on the empty tuple (fun i => i.elim0).

As in degree 0 the orientation is ±⟨·⟩ … so ∂T(g) = Σ m_i⟨g(x_i)⟩”), stated for an arbitrary compactly supported integer multiplicity 0-current S. (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum, whose accepted sub-lemmas may be reused by exact name.)
1. Let R = (M₀, θ, ζ) be an IMRep of S in ℝ^P (degree 0). H⁰ := μHE[0] equals μH[0] (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), so H⁰({x}) = 1 for every x (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence H⁰(t) = #t for every finite set t (sum_measure_singleton).
2. Carrier points have positive mass: for x ∈ M₀, R.measure({x}) = ∫⁻_{{x}} θ dH⁰⌞M₀ = θ(x)H⁰({x}) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, lintegral_singleton, field mult_pos).
3. M₀ ⊆ spt S. Let G := ℝ^P ∖ spt S; it is the zero region of S, a union of open sets, hence open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G has tsupport disjoint from spt S, so S(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence M_G(S) = 0. By (MR) (U = ℝ^P, W = G open), R.measure(G) = M_G(S) = 0. If x ∈ M₀ ∩ G, then R.measure({x}) ≤ R.measure(G) = 0, contradicting step 2. So M₀ ⊆ spt S.
4. M₀ is finite. By the field locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set spt S and step 3, ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ < ∞. If M₀ were infinite, then for every N ∈ ℕ there is a finite t ⊆ M₀ with #t = N (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq), and N = H⁰(t) = ∫⁻_t 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ (θ ≥ 1 on M₀); so ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ = ∞, a contradiction. Let F be the finite set M₀ (as a Finset).
5. The orientation is ±⟨·⟩ at every carrier point. Let B be the set of x for which no subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M₀ x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ(x)) Q. The field orients says H⁰(B ∩ M₀) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' for the measurable M₀). Since singletons have H⁰-measure 1, B ∩ M₀ = ∅. So for x ∈ M₀ there are Q and an orthonormal τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with ζ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α or ζ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α; as Fin 0 is empty, τ is the empty tuple ⟨⟩. Hence ζ(x)(α) = s(x)·α(⟨⟩) with s(x) ∈ {1, −1}.
6. Formula. For a test 0-form g, S(g) = R.action(g) = ∫_{M₀} θ(x)ζ(x)(g(x)) dH⁰(x). The integrand is integrable on the finite set M₀, each singleton having finite measure (integrableOn_singleton_iff, integrableOn_finset_iUnion), so ∫_{M₀} h dH⁰ = Σ_{x∈F} H⁰({x})·h(x) = Σ_{x∈F} h(x) (setIntegral_finset). With step 5, S(g) = Σ_{x∈F} s(x)θ(x)·g(x)⟨⟩. Put m(x) := s(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ for x ∈ F and m(x) := 0 otherwise. By step 3, F = M₀ ⊆ spt S. ∎
proof_key_steps: μHE[0] gives mass 1 to every point, so every carrier point has positive R.measure.
(VO) gives M_{ℝ^P∖spt S}(S) = 0, so by (MR) the carrier lies in spt S.
Local integrability of θ ≥ 1 on the compact spt S makes the carrier finite.
The a.e. orientation condition holds at every carrier point, so ζ(x) = ±⟨·⟩.
The integral over the finite carrier is the finite sum S(g) = Σ ±θ(x)g(x)⟨⟩.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the selected proof's step 5 (V4(i)), with all details supplied; Simon Ch. 6, 4.5(2)–(3) for the slicing identity behind (SL). The selected proof also assumes that X and ∂X have locally finite mass; this is not needed, because the IMRep measures used below are finite on compact sets. (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_slice_property_of_im, whose accepted sub-lemmas may be reused by exact name.) Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; M_W(X) := X.massOn W.
Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of X and ∂X, and let f be L-Lipschitz. Then f is continuous and E_t := {f < t} is a Borel set for every t (measurableSet_lt).
1. Slices. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P (open), k := d, T := X and μ, μ', ξ, ξ', f, L; its hypotheses are exactly the admissibility assumptions (finiteness on compact subsets, a.e. strong measurability, a.e. bounds, the two representation formulas) and the Lipschitz property. It yields currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{E_t} ξ'(η) dμ' for all test forms, such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t satisfies M_G(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open G and every t.
2. Z_t has locally finite mass for a.e. t. Fix k, m ∈ ℕ and apply (MM) with the constant sequence μ_j := μ, G := B_k(0) (open ball), (a, b) := (−m, m), L, and Z_j(t) := M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) for all j. Its hypotheses hold: f is continuous; μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ μ(B̄_k(0)) < ∞ since closed balls are compact; and for t ∈ (−m, m), Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_h h⁻¹μ(B_k(0) ∩ {t−h<f<t}) by step 1. (MM) gives a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m) and ∫_{(−m,m)} g ≤ L·liminf_j μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m<f<m}). The sequences are constant, so liminf_j Z_j(t) = M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) and the bound is L·μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m<f<m}) < ∞ (Filter.liminf_const). A measurable function with finite integral over (−m, m) is finite a.e. there (ae_lt_top for volume.restrict (−m, m), then ae_restrict_iff'). Hence for a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) ⇒ M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞. Intersecting these countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff over m, then over k) and taking m > |t|, we get a Lebesgue-null set N such that M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for all k ∈ ℕ and all t ∉ N. If W is open with compact closure, then W is bounded, W ⊆ B_k(0) for some k, and M_W(Z_t) ≤ M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for t ∉ N (massOn_mono). Fix t ∉ N for steps 3–8.
3. Integrals against IMRep measures. Let R = (M_R, θ, ζ) be an IMRep in ℝ^P of degree q and ν := R.measure = (H^q⌞M_R) with density θ. (i) For compact K, ν(K) = ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ K} θ dH^q < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, field locallyIntegrable_mult). (ii) ν ≪ H^q⌞M_R (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous); hence ζ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient, AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac) and, by (IMC)(d), |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for ν-a.e. x and all α (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). (iii) For every Borel E and every q-form ω, ∫_E ζ(ω) dν = ∫_{M_R ∩ E} θ·ζ(ω) dH^q: indeed ν⌞E = ((H^q⌞M_R)⌞E) with density θ (restrict_withDensity) = (H^q⌞(E ∩ M_R)) with density θ (Measure.restrict_restrict), and ∫ h d(λ with density θ) = ∫ θ·h dλ for the measurable ℝ≥0-valued density x ↦ θ(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul with f := fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ≥0); no integrability is needed). With E = ℝ^P this gives ∫ ζ(ω) dν = R.action(ω).
4. A_t is integer multiplicity. Let R_X be an IMRep of X. (IMC)(b) with E := E_t (Borel) gives a current A' and an IMRep R' representing A' with carrier M_{R_X} ∩ E_t, multiplicity θ_X and orientation ζ_X. Apply (RU) with k := d + 1, U := ℝ^P, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ, ξ), (μ₂, ξ₂) := (R_X.measure, ζ_X), (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): the finiteness, measurability and bound hypotheses hold by admissibility of (μ, ξ), by step 3(i)(ii), and trivially for the zero measure; the identity ∫ξ(ω)dμ = ∫ζ_X(ω)dR_X.measure + ∫0 d0 holds because both sides equal X(ω) (admissibility; step 3(iii) with E = ℝ^P and R_X.Represents X). (RU) with B := E_t and then step 3(iii) with E := E_t give, for every ω, A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t} ξ(ω) dμ = ∫_{E_t} ζ_X(ω) dR_X.measure = ∫_{M_{R_X} ∩ E_t} θ_X ζ_X(ω) dH^{d+1} = R'.action(ω). So R' represents A_t and A_t is integer multiplicity.
5. B_t is integer multiplicity: the same argument with an IMRep R_∂ of ∂X (degree d), the pair (μ', ξ') and (RU) with k := d shows that the IMRep obtained from R_∂ by (IMC)(b) with E := E_t represents B_t.
6. ∂A_t is integer multiplicity. Let W be open with compact closure. (i) M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(closure W) < ∞: for a W-admissible η (tsupport η ⊆ W, |η(x)| ≤ 1), η(x) = 0 for x ∉ closure W, so |ξ'(x)(η(x))| ≤ |η(x)| ≤ 1_{closure W}(x) for μ'-a.e. x, and ofReal(B_t(η)) ≤ ‖∫_{E_t} ξ'(η) dμ'‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{E_t} ‖ξ'(η)‖ₑ dμ' ≤ ∫⁻_{E_t} 1_{closure W} dμ' ≤ μ'(closure W) (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, lintegral_mono_ae, lintegral_indicator_one); take the supremum over η. (ii) M_W(Z_t) < ∞ by step 2. (iii) ∂A_t(η) = 1·Z_t(η) + 1·B_t(η) for every η, so the sibling current_algebra (Lean name cbr_cc_current_algebra), part (b), gives M_W(∂A_t) ≤ M_W(Z_t) + M_W(B_t) < ∞. Now BR(d) with U := ℝ^P and R := A_t (integer multiplicity by step 4) shows that ∂A_t is integer multiplicity.
7. Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) (ℝ^P is open; steps 5 and 6).
8. Conclusion. Let t ∉ N and let A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. Then A and A_t, and B and B_t, agree on all test forms, so A = A_t and B = B_t (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and ∂A − B = Z_t is integer multiplicity by step 7. Since N is null, this holds for L¹-a.e. t; as (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') and f were arbitrary, X has the integer slice property. ∎
proof_key_steps: (SL) provides slice currents A_t, B_t of X and the liminf bound for M_G(∂A_t − B_t).
(MM) with constant sequences and a countable intersection: for a.e. t, ∂A_t − B_t has locally finite mass.
IMRep measures are admissible and ∫_E ζ dR.measure = ∫_{M∩E} θζ dHⁿ; with (IMC)(b) and (RU) this makes A_t and B_t integer multiplicity.
M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(closure W) and current_algebra (b) give locally finite M(∂A_t); BR(d) makes ∂A_t IM and (IMC)(c) makes ∂A_t − B_t IM.
Any A, B with the slice formulas equal A_t, B_t, so X has the integer slice property.

Source: the selected proof's step 3, case n = 1 (the segment currents [[x₀, x]]); Simon Ch. 6, 2.2 (the current [[M]] of an oriented submanifold) and 3.1. Uses the siblings support_vanish (Lean name rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish), imrep_current (dtc_imrep_current) and current_algebra (cbr_cc_current_algebra), parts (a) and (b). Unlike the selected proof, a = b is allowed; then S = 0. (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_segment_current, whose accepted sub-lemmas may be reused by exact name.)
Case a = b.
1. Take S := 0. It is integer multiplicity by current_algebra (a); ∂0(g) = 0 = g(a)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩; current_algebra (b) with A = B = C = 0 and p = q = 0 gives M(0) = M_{ℝ^P}(0) = 0 < ∞; and 0 vanishes on every test form, so support_vanish (U := ℝ^P, K := {a}) gives spt 0 ⊆ {a} = [a, a] (segment_same).
Case a ≠ b.
2. Parametrization. Let ℓ := |b − a| > 0, τ := ℓ⁻¹(b − a) (so |τ| = 1) and φ(u) := a + uτ (u ∈ ℝ). φ is an isometry ℝ → ℝ^P (|φ(u) − φ(v)| = |u − v|), hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding); φ(0) = a and φ(ℓ) = b. Put I := φ((0, ℓ)), the open segment. I is Borel (the image of a Borel set under a measurable embedding), and I ⊆ [a, b] because φ(u) = a + (u/ℓ)(b − a) with u/ℓ ∈ [0, 1] (segment_eq_image').
3. H¹ on I. On ℝ, H¹ = μHE[1] is Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, finrank ℝ ℝ = 1). For the isometry φ the push-forward of H¹ is H¹⌞φ(ℝ) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure); restricting to I (Measure.restrict_map, and φ⁻¹(I) = (0, ℓ) by injectivity) gives H¹⌞I = φ_#(L¹⌞(0, ℓ)). Consequently H¹(I) = ℓ (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, Real.volume_Ioo) and ∫_I h dH¹ = ∫_{(0,ℓ)} h(a + uτ) du for every function h (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
4. Orientation. Let ζ₀ be the 1-vector α ↦ α(τ), i.e. ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ (fun _ => τ), and Q := span{τ}, a line (finrank_span_singleton). ζ₀ is a unit orientation of Q: the one-element family (τ) is orthonormal (|τ| = 1), its span is Q, and ζ₀(α) = α(τ) (IsUnitOrientationOf, first alternative).
5. Approximate tangent line at every point of I. Let x = φ(s₀) with 0 < s₀ < ℓ and δ := min(s₀, ℓ − s₀) > 0. For r > 0, blowUpMap x r sends φ(u) to r⁻¹(u − s₀)τ, so the image of I is contained in Q. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and choose ρ > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄_ρ(0). If 0 < r < δ/ρ and y = cτ ∈ Q has f(y) ≠ 0, then |c| = |y| ≤ ρ, so u := s₀ + rc satisfies |u − s₀| ≤ rρ < δ, hence u ∈ (0, ℓ) and y = blowUpMap x r (φ(u)) lies in the image of I. Thus f vanishes on Q ∖ blowUpMap x r '' I, and since Q is closed, ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' I} f dH¹ = ∫_Q f dH¹ for all r ∈ (0, δ/ρ) (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). The integrals are therefore eventually constant in 𝓝[>] 0 and converge to ∫_Q f dH¹; with finrank Q = 1 this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I x Q.
6. The IMRep R := (I, 1, ζ₀) in ℝ^P of degree 1. I is Borel and I ⊆ ℝ^P. I is countably 1-rectifiable: it lies in the range of F(v) := a + v₀τ on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1), which is 1-Lipschitz (|v₀ − w₀| ≤ |v − w|, PiLp.norm_apply_le), since φ(u) = F(EuclideanSpace.single 0 u) (countablyRectifiable_range, CountablyRectifiable.mono). subproblem.title: Compactly supported finite-mass IM filling of an IM boundary (V3)
subproblem.statement: Assume (MR), (IMC)(c), (VO) and (ISO). (MR): M_W(X) = R.measure(W) whenever R is an IMRep representing X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, W open (verbatim the (MR) hypothesis of the selected node's frozen Lean statement, the mass identity of dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support). (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the difference A − B is integer multiplicity (the third component of the selected node's (IMC) hypothesis). (VO): S(ω) = 0 for every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S (verbatim the (VO) hypothesis of the selected node, the frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support). (ISO) is the conclusion of the frozen statement of the selected node's sibling dependency isoperimetric (Lean name dmcbr_isoperimetric_filling) after its (DT) hypothesis: for all P, m ∈ ℕ there is a real c ≥ 1 such that every integer multiplicity Z ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, ∂Z = 0 and M(Z) < ∞ equals ∂Y for an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with M(Y) ≤ c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z) and spt Y ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt Z) < 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}}. Let d, P ∈ ℕ and T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with spt T compact, M(∂T) < ∞ and ∂T integer multiplicity. Then there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y compact.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the selected proof's step 3 (V3: a compactly supported IM filling Y of ∂T, by the isoperimetric theorem when n = d + 1 ≥ 2 and by signed segments from a point when n = 1, the total multiplicity being zero by (VO)); Simon Ch. 6, 6.1 (isoperimetric theorem) and 8.2 (“the general case of the theorem follows from the special case when ∂T = 0”). Uses the siblings support_vanish (Lean name rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish), current_algebra (cbr_cc_current_algebra), segment_current (dmcbr_cc_segment_current) and zero_current_sum (dmcbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum). The selected proof takes the base point x₀ of the segments outside {x_1, …, x_N}; since segment_current also allows coincident endpoints, the base point 0 works in every case (including P = 0 and N = 0). (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_compact_im_filling.)
1. spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, and spt ∂T is compact. If η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) has tsupport disjoint from spt T, then tsupport(dη) ⊆ tsupport η (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂T(η) = T(dη) = 0 by (VO). support_vanish with U := ℝ^P and K := spt T (compact) gives spt ∂T ⊆ spt T and spt ∂T compact.
Case d = m + 1 ≥ 1.
2. Z := ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, has compact support (step 1), ∂Z = ∂∂T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary) and M(Z) < ∞. (ISO) with P and m gives c ≥ 1 and an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) = 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = Z = ∂T, M(Y) ≤ ofReal(c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z)) < ∞, and spt Y ⊆ thickening(r, spt Z) with r := 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}.
3. spt Y is compact: spt Z is compact, hence bounded, so thickening(r, spt Z) is bounded and its closure C is compact (ℝ^P is proper). If tsupport ω is disjoint from C, it is disjoint from spt Y, so Y(ω) = 0 by (VO); support_vanish with K := C gives that spt Y is compact.
Case d = 0.
4. By step 1 and zero_current_sum (with (MR) and (VO)) applied to the integer multiplicity, compactly supported ∂T ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P), there are a finite F ⊆ spt ∂T and integers m(x) with ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)g(x)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g.
5. Total multiplicity zero: Σ_{x∈F} m(x) = 0. Choose ρ > 0 with spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0) (spt T is compact, hence bounded). Let ψ be a smooth bump function with compact support and ψ = 1 on B̄_ρ(0) (ContDiffBump centred at 0 with radii ρ < 2ρ), and let g(y) := constOfIsEmpty(ψ(y)), the 0-form with g(y)⟨⟩ = ψ(y); g is smooth with compact support, so g ∈ 𝒟⁰(ℝ^P). For y ∈ B_ρ(0), ψ = 1 on a neighbourhood of y, so Dψ(y) = 0 and dg(y) = ofSubsingleton(Dψ(y)) = 0 (extDeriv_constOfIsEmpty). Hence the support of dg lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ B_ρ(0), so tsupport(dg) is disjoint from B_ρ(0) ⊇ spt T, and ∂T(g) = T(dg) = 0 by (VO). On the other hand F ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0) by step 1, so g(x)⟨⟩ = 1 for x ∈ F and ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x). Hence Σ_{x∈F} m(x) = 0.
6. Segments. Put a := 0 ∈ ℝ^P. For each x ∈ ℝ^P choose, by segment_current (with (MR)), an integer multiplicity S_x ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with ∂S_x(g) = g(x)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩ for all test 0-forms g, M(S_x) < ∞ and spt S_x ⊆ [a, x].
7. Combination. current_algebra (c), with (IMC)(c), U := ℝ^P (open), ι := ℝ^P, the finite set F, the currents S_x and the integers m(x), gives an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with Y(ω) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(ω) for all ω and M(Y) ≤ Σ_{x∈F}|m(x)|M(S_x) < ∞ (a finite sum of finite terms).
8. ∂Y = ∂T: for every test 0-form g, ∂Y(g) = Y(dg) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(dg) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)∂S_x(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)g(x)⟨⟩ − (Σ_{x∈F} m(x))g(a)⟨⟩ = ∂T(g) by steps 4–6; hence ∂Y = ∂T (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
9. spt Y is compact: C := ⋃_{x∈F}[a, x] is compact, being a finite union of segments, each the continuous image of [0, 1]. If tsupport ω ∩ C = ∅, then tsupport ω ∩ spt S_x = ∅ for each x ∈ F, so S_x(ω) = 0 by (VO) and Y(ω) = 0; support_vanish with K := C gives that spt Y is compact.
10. In both cases Y is integer multiplicity, ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y is compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: spt ∂T ⊆ spt T is compact ((VO) and support_vanish).
d ≥ 1: (ISO) applied to the cycle ∂T; the filling lies in a bounded thickening, so its support is compact.
d = 0: ∂T = Σ m(x)δ_x over a finite F ⊆ spt T (zero_current_sum), and Σ m(x) = 0 by testing with a bump form equal to 1 near spt T and (VO).
Y := Σ m(x)[[0, x]] (segment_current, current_algebra (c)) is IM with ∂Y = ∂T, finite mass and compact support.
